bootstrap.pairing: within a year, paired across zones and curves; between years, unpaired (no shared days)

invariant_flags.note: CLAUDE.md's pooled naive-dominance invariant, per zone-year. The per-day same-start oracle bound is a theorem and is asserted separately; it held everywhere. A flag here is a statement about a regime-year, is labelled wherever its capture ratio is reported, and belongs in PROGRESS.md as a FLAG.

manifest_cross_check.window_note: this cycle counts over the local market days of the year; C1's manifest counted over the fetched file's window, which starts at 00:00Z on 01-01. The local market year reaches one hour further back, so a difference of one negative hour is expected exactly when that hour cleared below zero — which is what `explained_by_boundary_hours` checks, hour by hour and price by price, rather than tolerating a mismatch

crisis_2022.pairing: unpaired (two years share no market day)
crisis_2022.baseline_note: a zone's baseline is the mean of its other evaluated years, with any thin-regime cell dropped: averaging a capture ratio whose denominator is a few hundred EUR into a baseline would make the crisis year look good for the wrong reason

pooled_across_cells.label: descriptive only — the cells share zones, years, one model and one specification, so this is not an interval-bearing statistic

eight_zone_log_spread_line.label: descriptive least squares over the eight non-outlier zones' usable cells; no interval is claimed for the coefficients

cutover_status.why_no_comparison: the cutover falls inside the sealed 2025 holdout, and config/data.yaml stops fetching at 2024, so there is no post-cutover row in this project to compare against. The flag is therefore a statement about the evaluated window, not a split: every price hour behind every number in C13 was served at 60-minute resolution (manifest resolution_seconds=3600 on all 54 zone-years) and falls before 2025-10-01. data/contracts.py carries the resolution-change detection that would catch a post-cutover file if a later cycle fetched one; PLAN.md C15+ keeps native 15-minute analysis as a labelled stretch goal that is never blended into these results.

note: PLAN.md C13. The per-year columns for 2020-2023 are this cycle's own walk-forward runs of the nine-zone comparable arm; the 2024 column is C12's committed per-day artefact, re-pooled and checked against the committed store rows. 2020-2023 are PLAN.md training years: the predictions are out-of-sample but the model configuration was chosen on 2024, so these years weaken 'one year decides too little' without being the configuration holdout 2025 will be.
